questions.summary: Which of the 22 contracts survive scrutiny, and do spec, eval-result, and artifact-ref get registered?
Is the ontology one Record contract with typed entry kinds (requirement, criterion, decision, piece, finding, question), or separate Spec, Plan, and Review contracts linked to the backbone?
Does the delivery plan fold into the Plan as optional pr_group, branch, and stack_order fields on pieces, with no grouping meaning one PR?
Which survival test decides public contracts: A (an LLM writes and code reads), B (a durable artifact), or C (either)? The backbone directive may make this moot.
Do execution results fold into Plan piece status and evidence, and does diagnosis become a Review kind? Both are agent proposals the user has not confirmed.
Is the compiled per-task context a projection over the wheypoint graph (ADK style) or a ready-queue selection (Beads style)?
What sets plan weight (omitted, inline, or full): a code-scored complexity as in Taskmaster, or an agent or user choice as in OpenSpec lite?
Under a one-Record model, how do spec prose and diagrams fit, given the 6000-character notes cap and the parent's open living-spec fork?
How does one generator emit both the agent writer view and the host-complete shape for each kind, per the wiki consolidation audit?
Does any external reader consume schemas.easy-cheese.dev, and do removed contract URIs need a deprecation path?
Do the fan-out-bound contracts (remediation-state, remediation-cure-observation, review-request, diagnosis-request, pr-plan) leave with the stack, pending the parent's fan-out fork?
Should Cook refuse legacy specs without a hardened source? It accepts them by design, as it did at base 0009f3fa.
